question: Let \(f\) be the unique function defined on the positive integers such that \[ \sum_{d\mid n} d\cdot f\left(\frac{n}{d}\right)=1 \] for all positive integers \(n,\) where the sum is taken over all positive divisors of \(n.\) What is \(f(2023)?\)
solution:
Since \(2023=7\cdot17^2\), the equation for \(f(2023)\) involves only values at its six divisors. We can find those values from smallest to largest.

Taking \(n=1\) gives \(f(1)=1\). For a prime \(p\), the only divisors are \(1\) and \(p\), so
\[
f(p)+pf(1)=1,
\qquad f(p)=1-p.
\]
Thus \(f(7)=-6\) and \(f(17)=-16\).

Next, use the divisors of \(17^2=289\):
\[
f(289)+17f(17)+289f(1)=1.
\]
Therefore
\[
f(289)=1-17(-16)-289=-16.
\]
For \(119=7\cdot17\), we similarly obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(119)
&=1-7f(17)-17f(7)-119f(1)\\
&=1-7(-16)-17(-6)-119\\
&=96.
\end{aligned}
\]
Finally, the six divisors of \(2023\) are \(1,7,17,119,289,2023\). Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
1={}&f(2023)+7f(289)+17f(119)\\
&\quad+119f(17)+289f(7)+2023f(1)\\
={}&f(2023)+7(-16)+17(96)\\
&\quad+119(-16)+289(-6)+2023\\
={}&f(2023)-95.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(f(2023)=\boxed{96}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
The term with \(d=1\) is \(f(n)\), while every other term uses a smaller input. Thus the identity determines the function one value at a time, and verifying a formula for all inputs will identify \(f\).

Define
\[
g(1)=1,
\qquad g(n)=\prod_{p\mid n}(1-p),
\]
where the product includes each distinct prime divisor \(p\) of \(n\) once. We will check that \(g\) satisfies the given divisor identity.

Write \(n=p_1^{e_1}\cdots p_r^{e_r}\). Every divisor is obtained by independently choosing the exponent of each prime. For one prime power \(p^e\), choosing the exponent \(j\) of \(p\) in \(d\) contributes \(p^j(1-p)\) when \(j<e\), because \(p\) still divides \(n/d\). When \(j=e\), the contribution is \(p^e\), because \(p\) no longer divides \(n/d\).

Consequently, expanding a product of these independent choices gives
\[
\sum_{d\mid n}d\,g(n/d)
=\prod_{i=1}^r\left[(1-p_i)(1+p_i+\cdots+p_i^{e_i-1})+p_i^{e_i}\right].
\]
The finite geometric-sum identity gives
\[
(1-p)(1+p+\cdots+p^{e-1})+p^e
=1-p^e+p^e=1.
\]
Every factor is therefore \(1\), so the divisor sum equals \(1\). The case \(n=1\) also holds by the definition of \(g(1)\). Thus \(g=f\).

Since \(2023=7\cdot17^2\), its distinct prime divisors are \(7\) and \(17\), giving
\[
f(2023)=(1-7)(1-17)=(-6)(-16)=\boxed{96}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutionMethods.label: Verify a prime-product formula
